issues.description: Template `dd.py` declares `DD.weight` as `float`, but the rest of the code (including terminal constants) and the reference solution treat DD edge weights as complex amplitudes (`np.complex128`). This type mismatch is inconsistent with quantum-state amplitudes and can mislead students and break type checking in student implementations that correctly use complex numbers.
issues.suggestedFix: In `template_repository/dd.py`, change the `DD.weight` type annotation from `float` to `np.complex128` to match the intended complex-valued weights (as used by `ZERO_TERM`/`ONE_TERM` and the solution).

issues.description: In the tensor-network part of the problem statement, the number of qubits is referred to as `n` in some tasks, while other parts (and the template/solution function signatures) consistently use `num_qubits`. This mixed naming can confuse students into thinking `n` and `num_qubits` are different quantities.
issues.suggestedFix: Update `problem_statement.md` tensor-network section to consistently use `num_qubits` (and match casing) wherever referring to the number of qubits, aligning with `tensor_networks.py` function signatures.
